*thinking as the farmer*

Alright, let me think through this year. I've been doing wheat-maize on these 8 mu for 20 years now, so most of it I do the same way every year — no point changing what works. My husband helps some but he's away at construction work a lot, so it's mostly me and hired help when I can't manage alone.

**The wheat (already in the ground from last October)**

I planted the wheat back in mid-October like always, after I cleared the maize stalks. I used seed I bought from the agro shop in town — the shopkeeper sells what everyone around here uses, some variety called Jimai or Shimai, I don't remember exactly which one this year. Maybe 15 kg of seed per mu, cost me around 60 yuan per mu. I put down compound fertilizer before planting — 2 bags for the whole 8 mu, that's one of those 40 kg bags of 15-15-15, so about 10 kg per mu as base. 

Now in spring it's time to topdress. My neighbor lady who farms next to me, she said last year she put less urea because the price went up, and her wheat still came out okay. But I got scared last year when mine looked a bit yellow at jointing, so I put extra urea — maybe one and a half bags of urea across the 8 mu for topdressing. That's around 8-9 kg urea per mu at green-up, which works out to about 4 kg N. With my base fert, total N is maybe 15-16 kg per mu. I'd rather spend a little extra on fertilizer than watch my wheat come up short — losing 50 kg of yield hurts more than the 30 yuan of extra fertilizer.

For water, I'll irrigate at green-up in March, then again at jointing, and if May is dry I'll do one more before it fills out. Pumping from the well costs money — maybe 25-30 yuan per mu per time — so I try not to do more than I need. If the rain comes I skip one.

Spraying — I'll do one herbicide spray in spring for the broadleaf weeds, maybe one aphid spray in May if I see them. I don't spray fungicide unless I see something bad, can't afford to spray for nothing.

Last year I got about 430 kg per mu, the year before maybe 400. I'm expecting similar this year, around 420-450 if the spring rain is normal.

**The maize (after wheat)**

Once I harvest wheat in early June I need to get maize in the ground fast — neighbors all plant within a week of wheat harvest. I don't have my own machinery so I hire the man in the village with the no-till planter, he charges around 25-30 yuan per mu to plant right through the stubble. That's how most of us do it now — no time to plow.

I buy hybrid maize seed from the same shop, Zhengdan or Denghai type, whatever they're selling. About 3-4 kg per mu, costs around 30 yuan per mu. I put compound fertilizer with the planter, maybe 25 kg per mu of 15-15-15. Then I topdress with urea at the big-trumpet stage, around one bag (40 kg) for 8 mu, so 5 kg urea per mu. Total N works out to around 14 kg per mu.

Maize doesn't need as much water as wheat — usually I irrigate once or twice if July-August is dry, but most years the summer rain is enough. If it rains proper I don't irrigate at all and save the money.

I'll spray herbicide once after planting for the grasses and weeds. If I see the stem borer getting bad I'll spray, but usually I just pull a few bad plants and that's enough.

Last year I got around 480 kg per mu of maize. Should be similar this year.

**Labor and money**

Mostly it's me in the field. My husband comes back for busy times — planting and harvest. I might pay for 3-4 days of hired help at harvest time, around 150 yuan a day now, which is a lot but I can't carry it all alone at my age.

Total for seeds, fertilizer, pumping water, spray, hired planter, hired harvest help — I figure this year will run me around 600-650 yuan per mu across the two crops combined. On 8 mu that's 5,000 yuan or so in cash out before I sell anything. Tight but manageable if prices hold.
